proof.text: All inverse images and open extensions used below are exact constant-$\Lambda$ module functors. For the etale inverse images use exactness on abelian sheaves: kernels and cokernels of constant-$\Lambda$ module maps have their underlying abelian kernels and cokernels, with the induced scalar action, so the same assertion holds for modules. Pro-etale module inverse image is exact by the constant-coefficient exactness theorem. The comparison $C_T$ is the exact module inverse image specified in the pro-etale module definition. Etale extension by zero is exact, and pro-etale extension by zero is exact and acts degreewise. The two open-adjunction pairs are $j_{e,!}\dashv j_e^*$ and $j_{p,!}\dashv j_p^*$, and likewise for $j'$. Here and below all pro-etale module pullbacks use the canonical constant-ring identifications of the cited exactness theorem.

proof.text: Use the termwise derived functors of these exact functors. The exact-functor factorization theorem says that they preserve quasi-isomorphisms and compute the derived functors on every complex. A natural transformation on sheaves gives a chain map on each complex: its naturality at $d^n$ is precisely the chain-map equation in degree $n$. The localization universal property descends these transformations, preserving composition, inverses, and equalities. In particular the open units and counits descend. Their two triangle equations hold degreewise on complexes, hence after localization; thus they give the canonical derived open adjunctions. Every sheaf-level equation used below therefore holds on derived categories with these specified maps. Exact functors preserve cohomological lower bounds by the bounded-below theorem, so all functors in this argument restrict to the $D^+$ categories in the statement.

proof.text:
Write $J_e=j_{e,!}$, $I_e=j_e^*$, $J_p=j_{p,!}$, $I_p=j_p^*$, and use primes for $j'$. Write $u_e:1\to I_eJ_e$, $u_p:1\to I_pJ_p$ for the open units. The open-comparison unit theorem gives
$$I_p(e_{j,M})\circ a_{j,J_eM}\circ C_U(u_{e,M})=u_{p,C_UM}.$$
It applies to the same finite ring and the same specified $a_j,e_j$, and Step 2 descends its sheaf equation. Multiplying by $I_p(e_{j,M}^{-1})$ shows that the $J_p\dashv I_p$ transpose of $e_{j,M}^{-1}$ is $a_{j,J_eM}\circ C_U(u_{e,M})$. This is the transpose of the inverse mate of $a_j$ in the mate definition. Injectivity of this Hom bijection shows that $e_j^{-1}:J_pC_U\to C_ZJ_e$ has right mate $a_j:C_UI_e\to I_pC_Z$, with respect to $J_e\dashv I_e$ and $J_p\dashv I_p$. The same argument for $j'$ gives $(e_{j'}^{-1})^\flat=a_{j'}$.

proof.text: Let $h_e:I'_eq_e^*\xrightarrow{\sim}r_e^*I_e$ and $h_p:I'_pq_p^*\xrightarrow{\sim}r_p^*I_p$ be the canonical pullback-square identifications, and put $c_e=h_e^{-1}$, $c_p=h_p^{-1}$. Put $d_e=(\beta^e)^{-1}$ and $d_p=(\beta^p)^{-1}$. The etale base-change theorem specifies the $J'_e\dashv I'_e$ transpose of $d_{e,M}$ as $c_{e,J_eM}\circ r_e^*(u_{e,M})$. Its module-complex assertion and the derived corollary give this same named arrow on $D^+$. For the pro-etale map the open-tensor normalization theorem, specialized to the finite constant ring $\Lambda$, explicitly identifies its $\beta$ with the canonical map of the pro-etale base-change theorem and specifies exactly the analogous transpose $c_{p,J_pN}\circ r_p^*(u_{p,N})$. Thus, by the inverse-mate formula, $d_e:J'_er_e^*\to q_e^*J_e$ has mate $c_e$, and $d_p:J'_pr_p^*\to q_p^*J_p$ has mate $c_p$. This uses the normalization clause of the cited theorem, not just invertibility of its comparison.

proof.text:
The Cartesian coherence clause of the pullback-comparison theorem, written with the inverse square comparisons $c_e,c_p$, is the equality
$$ (I'_pa_q)\circ(a_{j'}q_e^*)\circ(C_{U'}c_e)
=(c_pC_Z)\circ(r_p^*a_j)\circ(a_rI_e).\tag{*}$$
Both sides go from $C_{U'}r_e^*I_e$ to $I'_pq_p^*C_Z$. Indeed the left path compares $r_e^*I_e$ with $I'_eq_e^*$ first and then moves $C$ past $j'$ and $q$; the right path moves $C$ past $r$ and $j$ first and then uses the pro-etale square comparison. This is the cited Cartesian compatibility with its orientation reversed, using the inverses of $h_e,h_p$. The comparisons include the chosen Cartesian-square datum, so no strict equality of chosen fibre products is assumed. Step 2 descends this sheaf-level equality to the same derived functors.

proof.text:
Take mates between $J_e\dashv I_e$ and $J'_p\dashv I'_p$, with side functors $G=C_{U'}r_e^*$ and $H=q_p^*C_Z$. Consider
$$A=(q_p^*e_j^{-1})\circ(d_pC_U)\circ(J'_pa_r):J'_pC_{U'}r_e^*\to q_p^*C_ZJ_e.$$
Pasting the square $e_j^{-1}$ with the square $d_p$ gives, by the mate-pasting theorem and Steps 3--4, the mate $(c_pC_Z)\circ(r_p^*a_j)$ for the composite before precomposing $J'_pa_r$. Precomposition by $J'_pa_r$ precomposes its mate by $a_rI_e$. To check this last whiskering directly in the mate formula, naturality of the unit of $J'_p\dashv I'_p$ at $a_r$ moves $a_r$ through that unit; the remaining two factors are unchanged. Consequently
$$A^\flat=(c_pC_Z)\circ(r_p^*a_j)\circ(a_rI_e).$$

proof.text:
For the same two adjunctions and side functors consider
$$B=(a_qJ_e)\circ(C_{Z'}d_e)\circ(e_{j'}^{-1}r_e^*):J'_pC_{U'}r_e^*\to q_p^*C_ZJ_e.$$
Paste $d_e$ and $e_{j'}^{-1}$ in the opposite order to Step 6. The mate-pasting theorem and Steps 3--4 give $(a_{j'}q_e^*)\circ(C_{U'}c_e)$ for the composite before postcomposing $a_qJ_e$. Postcomposing that square by $a_qJ_e$ postcomposes its mate by $I'_pa_q$. In the defining mate formula, this follows by naturality of $a_q:C_{Z'}q_e^*\to q_p^*C_Z$ at the counit $J_eI_e\to1$: it moves $a_q$ past the last counit factor. Thus
$$B^\flat=(I'_pa_q)\circ(a_{j'}q_e^*)\circ(C_{U'}c_e).$$

proof.text:
Equation (*) identifies the two mates computed in Steps 6--7. Since the mate correspondence is a bijection, $A=B$. Postcompose this equality with $q_p^*e_j$ and precompose with $e_{j'}r_e^*$. The adjacent $e_j,e_j^{-1}$ and $e_{j'},e_{j'}^{-1}$ cancel, leaving
$$d_p\circ(J'_pa_r)\circ(e_{j'}r_e^*)=(q_p^*e_j)\circ(a_qJ_e)\circ C_{Z'}d_e,$$
that is, $d_p\circ T=S\circ C_{Z'}d_e$. Postcompose by $\beta^p$ and precompose by $C_{Z'}\beta^e$, and cancel each inverse pair $\beta^p d_p=1$ and $d_e\beta^e=1$. Evaluation at $M$ gives precisely
$$\beta^p_{C_UM}\circ S_M=T_M\circ C_{Z'}(\beta^e_M).$$
All equations take place in the actual derived Hom sets with the comparisons fixed above. The Noetherian and qcqs assumptions of the item remain in force; no direct-image comparison or conservativity of geometric pro-etale stalks is needed in this open-adjunction calculation.

title: Site comparison preserves the named open base-change map
statement:
Fix a finite commutative ring $\Lambda$. Use ordinary bounded-below derived categories of constant-$\Lambda$ modules on small etale and pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Write $C_T=\nu_T^*$ for the exact site comparison [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. For a qcqs morphism $u:U\to V$ write $a_u:C_Uu_e^*\xrightarrow{\sim}u_p^*C_V$ for the canonical pullback comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback], $b_u:C_VRu_{e,*}\xrightarrow{\sim}Ru_{p,*}C_U$ for its counit-mate direct-image comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate], and for an open immersion $j$ write $e_j:C j_{e,!}\xrightarrow{\sim}j_{p,!}C$ for the canonical adjoint open-extension comparison [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison, def-cbc-finite-constant-coefficient-transport]. Subscripts $e,p$ distinguish the two sites. Let $j:U\hookrightarrow Z$ and $j':U'\hookrightarrow Z'$ be open immersions in a Cartesian square with $q:Z'\to Z$ and $r:U'\to U$ [def-cbc-open-immersion-square]. Assume all four schemes are Noetherian, meaning that each has a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and all four arrows are qcqs. Let $\beta^e:q_e^*j_{e,!}\xrightarrow{\sim}j'_{e,!}r_e^*$ be the canonical etale open base-change map [lem-cbc-extension-zero-base-change], and $\beta^p:q_p^*j_{p,!}\xrightarrow{\sim}j'_{p,!}r_p^*$ the canonical pro-etale one [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-base-change]. For $M\in D^+(U_e,\Lambda)$ put
$$S_M=q_p^*(e_{j,M})\circ a_{q,j_{e,!}M},\qquad T_M=j'_{p,!}(a_{r,M})\circ e_{j',r_e^*M}.$$
Then the equality of actual derived morphisms is
$$\beta^p_{C_UM}\circ S_M=T_M\circ C_{Z'}(\beta^e_M).$$
